title: Behold, National Parks!
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the history and idea of U.S. national parks, starting with Yellowstone's 1872 designation as the world's first national park. They cover Yosemite's origins in the 1851 Mariposa Battalion and its name, the early state park and federal protection of Yosemite, Hot Springs as an earlier federal reservation, Yellowstone's founding under Ulysses S. Grant, early mismanagement and the Army's role under Philip Sheridan, the 1916 creation of the National Park Service, John Muir and Theodore Roosevelt, the Grand Canyon and Ralph Henry Cameron's fight over the Bright Angel Trail, the 1920s-30s eastern parks funded by John D. Rockefeller Jr. and the CCC, Mission 66, the 1963 Leopold Report, wolf reintroduction and trophic cascades, geodiversity, economic value of parks, park death statistics, and the spread of national parks worldwide. The episode ends with listener mail.

segments.title: Opening banter and Yellowstone anniversary
segments.summary: Hosts open with casual banter, then note the 150th anniversary of Yellowstone as the first national park, and discuss Wallace Stegner's 'America's best idea' quote and the idea of setting land aside.

segments.title: Camping and early Yosemite history
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh discuss dispersed camping in national parks and their travels. They then cover the Mariposa Battalion's 1851 entry into Yosemite Valley, the naming of Yosemite after the Ahwahnechee, and the meaning of the name.

segments.title: Yosemite as state park and Hot Springs
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the displacement of Native Americans tied to park creation, the possibility of renaming Yosemite, and Senator Conness's bill that set aside Yosemite Valley as a state park signed by Lincoln. They note Hot Springs, Arkansas as an earlier federal reservation.

segments.title: Founding of Yellowstone
segments.summary: Cornelius Hedges proposed a public park for the 1870 Washington expedition area; because the land spanned multiple territories, federal action followed, and Ulysses S. Grant signed the Yellowstone Park Protection Act on March 1, 1872.

segments.title: Early mismanagement and the Army
segments.summary: Early Yellowstone faced concessionaire problems under the Yellowstone Park Improvement Company. General Philip Sheridan sent the Army to manage the park from 1886 to 1916, and the ranger uniform's cavalry resemblance and green color are discussed. Josh offers a capitalism and stewardship reflection.

segments.title: John Muir, Roosevelt, and the 1916 National Park Service
segments.summary: Muir lobbied for Yosemite, and after a camping trip with Theodore Roosevelt, the park expanded. Roosevelt designated many monuments. Congress created the National Park Service through the Organic Act of 1916, signed by Woodrow Wilson.

segments.title: Grand Canyon and Ralph Henry Cameron
segments.summary: The hosts describe Senator Ralph Henry Cameron's control of Bright Angel Trail and land near the Grand Canyon, his defiance of Congress and the Supreme Court, and his defeat after an LA Times investigation. The Grand Canyon then became a fully unfettered national park. Criteria for national park status and geodiversity are also discussed.

segments.title: Rockefeller, CCC, Mission 66, and Leopold Report
segments.summary: Eastern national parks were established in the 1920s and 1930s, funded by John D. Rockefeller Jr. and built by Civilian Conservation Corps labor. After WWII, Mission 66 expanded visitor centers. The 1963 Leopold Report led to wildlife protection, and the wolf reintroduction to Yellowstone and trophic cascades are discussed.

segments.title: Park economics, safety statistics, and global spread
segments.summary: The hosts cite visitor spending and economic return, discuss the perception that parks are dangerous while noting low death rates, mention North Cascades' high death rate, and trace the spread of national parks from Australia's Royal National Park to Canada, New Zealand, Europe, and Africa, closing with Sierra Club's proposal for more parks.
